newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr motors on and up,Eurobourses look sickly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr motors on and up,Eurobourses look sickly.

text.p: The dollar started bullishly in Europe on Tuesday, hitting new highs against the mark, yen and Swiss franc but bourses were mainly weaker following another overnight fall on Wall Street.
The dollar touched a 31-month high of 1.6565 marks and a 47-month peak of 120.53 yen and analysts said said it could surge higher if there was a strong showing in Tuesday's U.S. employment cost data.

"People are speculating perhaps we'll get strong data today and that's helping the dollar as well... as that could raise the chances of an early Fed rate hike," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
By 0945 GMT, the U.S. currency had subsided to 1.6520 marks and 120.40 yen, which was still a pfenning and a yen above late Monday European levels of 1.6413 marks and 119.43 yen.

"If we get the employment cost index reported above one percent, we will have good cause for concern and the market will take the dollar higher," said PaineWebber chief international economist Michael O'Hanlon.

A Reuters poll of economists showed the that U.S. cost employment index for the fourth quarter of 1996, due at 1330 GMT, was on average expected to rise 0.9 percent after a 0.6 percent increase previously.

The index was seen as key to any decision by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on interest rates at its meeting next week, especially after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan warned of risks of wage-driven inflation in his testimony to the U.S. Senate Budget Committee last week.
Meanwhile, analysts said the dollar was also helped by reports that neither Germany nor Japan appeared very worried about the dollar's strength against their currencies.
"They (Japanese authorities) don't see it as a major problem because they see it as a case of a strong dollar rather than a weak yen," Rayner said.
On the bourses, leading London shares were a third of a percentage point weaker after U.S. blue chips again slid overnight, by 35 points, following their near 60-point setback on Friday.
London was expected to trade in a narrow range during the morning session as investors awaited the U.S. data and Wall Street's open.
"It's pretty quiet. People aren't too interested in doing any business until we see these U.S. wage numbers," the head of trading at a major investment bank said.

"Today's U.S. Q4 employment cost index is one of the most important economic releases of the week, if not the year if it marks a possible turning point in Fed monetary policy," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in his daily outlook on Tuesday.

German shares also slipped in pre-bourse electronic trading and opened lower in floor business, pulled down by the softer Wall Street but partially supported by the strength of the dollar, which is positive for German exports.

The Paris bourse was the exception, managing to move into positive territory with the dollar's rise to more than 5.58 francs offsetting the negative effect of falling U.S. stocks and a bond market drop.
CURRENCIES AT 0945 GMT
The dollar was at 120.40 yen and 1.6520 marks compared with late Europe's Monday level of 119.43 yen and 1.6413 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0945 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 17.1 points lower at 4,194.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 4.93 at 2,440.5.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 8.23 at 2,986.3.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened in London at $356.90 compared with London's monday close of $354.60. Silver was stronger too at $5.04.
